proof_scope: Pi extension feature coverage for lazy-report-shame-shame-shame: mandatory Status Report rendering, strict footer checking, empty tool-turn skip, collaborative rejection notice, pending review packet, /shame show recovery, /shame review fallback, direct label JSONL capture, and one-retry behavior, and explicit $shame extension debug status reports without control-plane false positives, and external-owner reload blockers. Includes 50 WebGPT-derived adversarial status-report attack cases.

claims.proves: The installed-style Pi extension hooks and commands behave as the $shame contract requires under deterministic simulation. Proof[] paths are read back from disk before a done status can pass.
claims.does_not_prove: Every already-running Pi session has reloaded the extension, human label quality, or future classifier performance.

capability_claims.description: Tool-call-only assistant messages with no text are ignored and do not create pending review packets or retries.
Bad final status reports are replaced with a collaborative correction packet, write a pending review packet, and queue one retry.
/shame show and /shame review recover or explain the pending rejected candidate after reload/headless fallback.
The extension /shame command labels the raw rejected candidate as v2 JSONL training data.
The deterministic checker rejects missing footer, missing agentic-evals receipt, uncommitted relevant work, obvious next step, and active-goal non-status patterns.
An active continuation guard file with an open relevant agent-work ticket or unresolved gate rejects a premature final report and queues a follow-up; closed tickets and passed gates allow final.
The Pi shame extension trusts pi.agent_status.v1 data over model-authored What remains prose; continuing.not_done[].next_command queues the follow-up.
Every guarded report must end with pydantic-valid pi.agent_status.v1 JSON; the extension strips model-authored status prose/JSON and renders the visible Status Report from validated data.

A WebGPT-derived adversarial suite plus repeated blunt-review follow-up probes attacks Status Report ownership, label-bound JSON-to-prose projection, JSON validity, duplicate-key laundering, What-remains bypasses, CommonMark fence confusion, hidden HTML/reference laundering, validator fail-open behavior, state legality, and terminality.

After two same-fingerprint failed status reports, the Pi extension blocks another stale failure report unless the agent asks one plain human question, cites debugger.proof.v1, or cites an exact debugger failure handoff.
UNLAZY_FORCED_RETRY follow-up prompts keep the guard active and reject vague prose footers without final pi.agent_status.v1 JSON.
status validity is controlled by final pi.agent_status.v1 pydantic validation, not regex or agent-authored prose
The shame immutable goal is pydantic-validated and names each ecosystem component plus what it MUST do.
pydantic-valid done status cannot cite fake proof paths; proof[] entries must exist on disk
